prov_p161.name: Cúc Viên
prov_p161.lore: Flat steppe and grass on the northern coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, around the flower village that hid Phượng Minh's scouts in 586. Its people grow chrysanthemums for the palace's autumn rites and fish the shore. A warm spring at the village edge is banked with flowers.

prov_p162.name: Tang Âm
prov_p162.lore: Grass and low hills on the coast road where the silk caravans rest under the great mulberry. Its people keep inns, fodder yards and stables. A wood vein runs under the caravan yard, and carters say it is why the tree never ages.

prov_p163.name: Hồ Tâm
prov_p163.lore: Grass and bamboo behind the coastal dunes, around the round lake that breathes with the tide. Its people fish the lake and the sea. Giant crabs crowd the dune shore, and the villagers trap them for the markets.

prov_p164.name: Lô Châu
prov_p164.lore: Jungle, hills and reed marsh on a river in the west of Đan Huyệt Châu. Its people cut reed and have done so since before the pirates came. A forest of water pines grows along the river above the village.

prov_p44.name: Ngũ Thải
prov_p44.lore: Grass, jungle and bamboo at the river mouth around the five-coloured port city. Its people glaze tile, fish and trade along the coast. A fire vein near the city is where Hùng Phần Vũ is said to have first sat as a boy.

prov_p93.name: Thạch Cơ
prov_p93.lore: Flat grass and steppe on the northern gulf around the port that grew from the fleet's jetty. Its people work the ships and the shipyard. An earth vein under the shore is said to be why the jetty stood for four centuries before the storm.

prov_p94.name: Tang Điền
prov_p94.lore: Red-soiled grass and steppe on the coast, planted in mulberry since 200. Its people raise silkworms and reel silk, and the town belongs to Phần Vũ Đường. A vein runs under the red earth, and the silk women say it is what puts fire in the thread.

prov_phan_vu.name: Phần Vũ
prov_phan_vu.lore: Grass, jungle and steep volcanic ground on the east coast, where Phần Vũ Đường tempers its disciples in the vents and Chúc Dung Khẩu smokes over the sea. Few farm here; its people serve the hall and its burned. The walls of a fire-silk town that died with Xích Thành stand on the slope.

prov_r20_1.name: Tân Sinh
prov_r20_1.lore: Steppe and grass on the north coast below the red cliffs of Xích Thành Môn. Its people herd goats and dry fish, and do not graze the cliffs. The village was rebuilt on the ashes of one of the eleven villages Xích Thành burned.

prov_r20_10.name: Thạch Tượng
prov_r20_10.lore: Jungle, grass and red hills on the west coast around the quarry of Đan Thạch. Its people are quarrymen and masons who cut and dress the red stone. The burned walls of Xích Thành's old quarry town stand on the hillside above.

prov_r20_11.name: Thu Võng
prov_r20_11.lore: Jungle and grass on the southern coast, low and wet. Its people fish with nets and gather agarwood in the forest. Agarwood from here is burned in Phượng Minh's halls.

prov_r20_12.name: Hải Sâm
prov_r20_12.lore: Deep jungle down to a mangrove shore on the southern coast. Its people dive for sea cucumbers and dry them for the cities. A great python holds the jungle valley behind the village.

prov_r20_13.name: Tân Lang
prov_r20_13.lore: Jungle, grass and mangrove on the south coast. Its people grow areca palms and sell the nuts along the coast road. A wood vein lies in the jungle behind the groves.

prov_r20_14.name: Hương Liệu
prov_r20_14.lore: Low jungle on the south coast around a small spice market town. Its people gather and trade spices and resin from the jungle. Old banyans crowd the forest behind the town.

prov_r20_15.name: Sa Nhân
prov_r20_15.lore: Jungle and grass on the southern shore. Its people grow cardamom under the trees. On the shore stand the ruins of a sea hall of Xích Thành Môn, abandoned in 590.

prov_r20_16.name: Nam Tân
prov_r20_16.lore: A small, steep stretch of jungle and forest on the south-western coast with a good harbour. Its people work the boats that sail to the far south. Kapok trees flower red on the hill behind the town.

prov_r20_17.name: Đậu Khấu
prov_r20_17.lore: Jungle hills and mangrove on the far southern coast, near Thôn Hải's old islet. Its people grow nutmeg and fish. A spice town on the shore was burned by the pirates in 771.

prov_r20_18.name: Bằng Trình
prov_r20_18.lore: A small jungle coast in the far south-west facing the southern sea. Its fishers sail further south than any others on the coast. A water vein on the hill looks out toward where the great Bằng is said to fly.

prov_r20_19.name: Hồ Tiêu
prov_r20_19.lore: Jungle hills on the southern coast. Its people grow pepper vines on the trees and sell the dried berries to the ports. Dragon's blood trees grow on the slope above.

prov_r20_2.name: Lô Hội
prov_r20_2.lore: Grass, jungle and bamboo on the east coast just south of Phần Vũ Đường. Its people grow aloe and sell the salve to the hall's burned disciples. A fire vein in the grass still holds the warmth of the vents.

prov_r20_20.name: Hồng Sa
prov_r20_20.lore: A tiny grassy headland on the south coast with beaches of red sand. Its people fish and boil salt. A hot pool by the shore is warmed by the waves breaking over volcanic rock.

prov_r20_21.name: Thiên Nhai
prov_r20_21.lore: A tiny grassy cape at the south-western end of the coast. Its people run the last harbour before the open sea. Fire lizards hold the cliff beyond the town.

prov_r20_22.name: Thuận Phong
prov_r20_22.lore: Jungle and a little volcanic ground on the south coast, facing Đồ Nam Đảo, with the red spring Chu Sa Tuyền inland. Its people fish and sail. They are the ones who row out to leave fish in the great Bằng's hollow.

prov_r20_23.name: Phù Thạch
prov_r20_23.lore: Jungle on the flanks of a coastal volcano in the south. Its people gather pumice and fish. On the slope stand the lava-covered halls of a Xích Thành pavilion, and a vent above them still burns.

prov_r20_24.name: Bái Nhật
prov_r20_24.lore: Jungle and volcanic ground on the far south-east coast, facing Dục Nhật Đảo and bordering the snake forest of Vạn Xà Lâm. Its people fish and ferry pilgrims to the hermit Mạc Quy Khư. Every morning they bow to the sunrise over the island.

prov_r20_25.name: Phá Lãng
prov_r20_25.lore: Jungle on the far southern coast, facing the islet of Thôn Hải Môn. Its boatmen row treasure seekers out to dig in the burned hold, and some of them do not row back. Palms line the shore.

prov_r20_3.name: Trúc Lâu
prov_r20_3.lore: Wide grass and bamboo on the eastern coast. Its people live in raised bamboo houses and grow rice and mulberry. A young hall of fire-silk weavers has risen on the shore, and the elders of Phượng Minh watch it with interest and some unease.

prov_r20_4.name: Cam Giá
prov_r20_4.lore: Low grass and jungle on the south coast near the river. Its people grow sugarcane and boil it into brown sugar for the cities. A boiling spring in the fields is used to start the cane fires.

prov_r20_5.name: Lam Điện
prov_r20_5.lore: Grass and jungle on the south coast. Its people grow indigo and dye cloth and silk blue for the coast. A drowned town lies on the shore, lost to a storm tide in 913.

prov_r20_6.name: Lệ Chi
prov_r20_6.lore: Grass and jungle on the south-eastern coast. Its people grow lychees and send them to the cities by fast boat. A forest of flame trees burns red on the grass every summer.

prov_r20_7.name: Quế Viên
prov_r20_7.lore: Jungle with a mangrove shore on the south-eastern coast. Its people grow longans and dry them for the markets. A mangrove town on the shore was burned by Thôn Hải in 767.

prov_r20_8.name: Bạch Diêm
prov_r20_8.lore: Grass and jungle on the flat eastern coast. Its people make salt in pans and fish the shallows. A water vein lies among the mangrove roots inland.

prov_r20_9.name: Huyết Nham Lĩnh
prov_r20_9.lore: A block of high red mountain on the west coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, too steep for villages. Only quarrymen and fire cultivators climb it. Its summit is said to be where the five-coloured bird was seen over the vermilion caves.

prov_p161_hot_spring_1.name: Hoàng Cúc Thang
prov_p161_hot_spring_1.look: A warm pool at the village edge, banked so thick with yellow chrysanthemums that its steam smells of them.
prov_p161_hot_spring_1.lore: The villagers soak chrysanthemum heads in it for a tea they sell to Phượng Minh for the autumn rites.

prov_p162_spirit_vein_1.name: Tang Căn Mạch
prov_p162_spirit_vein_1.look: The dusty caravan yard under the great mulberry, where the ground stays cool even at noon.
prov_p162_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein runs under the yard. Carters say it is why the old tree never ages.

prov_p163_beast_lair_1.name: Cự Giải Chử
prov_p163_beast_lair_1.look: A flat grassy shore between the lake and the dunes, riddled with burrows and littered with broken shells as big as shields.
prov_p163_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit crabs with claws that can snap an oar live in the burrows. Hồ Tâm's villagers trap the small ones and leave the old ones alone.

prov_p164_forest_1.name: Thủy Tùng Lâm
prov_p164_forest_1.look: A grove of tall water pines on the wet grass by the river, their knobbed roots rising out of the mud like rows of kneeling stones.
prov_p164_forest_1.lore: Lô Châu's reed cutters take its wood for the stilts of their houses, since water pine does not rot in the marsh. When the village was rebuilt in 782, every new stilt came from this grove, and the stumps are still counted as its founders.

prov_p44_spirit_vein_1.name: Thải Vũ Mạch
prov_p44_spirit_vein_1.look: A low grass rise outside the city walls, where a small shrine holds a red feather under glass.
prov_p44_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein. The city says Hùng Phần Vũ first sat here as a boy, and its young come to sit where he sat.

prov_p93_spirit_vein_1.name: Bàn Thạch Huyệt
prov_p93_spirit_vein_1.look: A flat shelf of bedrock in the grass behind the harbour, with a ring of old fleet mooring stones set round it.
prov_p93_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Thổ (earth) vein lies under the rock. Sailors say it is why the old jetty stood for four centuries.

prov_p94_spirit_vein_1.name: Xích Nhưỡng Mạch
prov_p94_spirit_vein_1.look: A field of rust-red earth among the mulberry rows, warm underfoot on cold mornings.
prov_p94_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Thổ (earth) vein touched with fire. The silk women say it is what puts fire in the thread.

prov_phan_vu_ruin_1.name: Hỏa Ti Trấn
prov_phan_vu_ruin_1.look: Blackened walls on a steep slope above the vent field, with rows of stone reeling basins standing in the roofless halls.
prov_phan_vu_ruin_1.lore: Xích Thành Môn's town of fire-silk spinners, where the thread for the Xích Hà Kỳ was reeled from the vents. It burned in the fighting of 590 when Phượng Minh destroyed the gate, and no one has spun fire-silk there since.

prov_r20_1_village_1.name: Tân Sinh Thôn
prov_r20_1_village_1.look: A coast village of red-stone houses on steppe below the red cliffs, a blackened old hearthstone set at its centre.
prov_r20_1_village_1.lore: It was rebuilt on the ashes of one of the eleven villages Xích Thành burned, and its people keep the old hearthstone as a shrine. They herd goats and dry fish, and never graze the cliffs.

prov_r20_1_spirit_vein_2.name: Tàn Hỏa Mạch
prov_r20_1_spirit_vein_2.look: A patch of grass where the earth is cracked and faintly warm, a short walk from the ruined gate.
prov_r20_1_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein that once fed Xích Thành's fire arts. Phượng Minh keeps an eye on anyone who sits here too long.

prov_r20_10_village_1.name: Thạch Tượng Thôn
prov_r20_10_village_1.look: A village of red-stone houses below the quarry, its yards full of half-dressed blocks and chisel sheds.
prov_r20_10_village_1.lore: Its masons dress the red stone of Đan Thạch for Phượng Minh's builders, and their own houses are made of the blocks that cracked.

prov_r20_10_forest_2.name: Đan Mộc Lâm
prov_r20_10_forest_2.look: A grove of small thorny trees on the grass below the red quarry, their cut stumps showing heartwood as bright red as the stone above.
prov_r20_10_forest_2.lore: Its sappan wood is chipped and boiled for red dye and sold to the silk dyers of Tang Điền. The masons of Thạch Tượng say the trees drink the colour out of the red mountain.

prov_r20_10_ruin_3.name: Tạc Thạch Trấn
prov_r20_10_ruin_3.look: Burned walls on a red hillside above the quarry, the ground strewn with broken chisels.
prov_r20_10_ruin_3.lore: Xích Thành Môn's quarry town for Đan Thạch, burned in 588 in the War of the Vermilion Caves when the gate's men fired it rather than leave it. The quarrymen who stayed built Thạch Tượng below.

prov_r20_11_village_1.name: Thu Võng Thôn
prov_r20_11_village_1.look: A low shore village of stilted houses at the jungle's edge, long seine nets hanging on poles before every door and canoes drawn up on the grey sand.
prov_r20_11_village_1.lore: Its people haul seine nets from the beach at dawn, whole families on each rope, and in the dry season go into the forest behind for agarwood. The resin they bring out is burned in Phượng Minh's halls.

prov_r20_11_forest_2.name: Trầm Hương Lâm
prov_r20_11_forest_2.look: Dark jungle where some trunks are scarred and oozing black resin, and the air smells of incense.
prov_r20_11_forest_2.lore: Its agarwood is burned in Phượng Minh's halls. The gatherers wound a tree and wait twenty years before they cut it.

prov_r20_12_village_1.name: Hải Sâm Thôn
prov_r20_12_village_1.look: A village on the mangrove edge where dried sea cucumbers hang in strings under the eaves.
prov_r20_12_village_1.lore: Its divers bring sea cucumbers up from the shallows and dry them for the city kitchens.

prov_r20_12_beast_lair_2.name: Đại Mãng Cốc
prov_r20_12_beast_lair_2.look: A jungle valley where broad smooth tracks run through the undergrowth and shed skins hang from the branches.
prov_r20_12_beast_lair_2.lore: A python longer than a boat lives here and takes deer, pigs and the occasional diver. Alchemists pay well for its shed skin.

prov_r20_13_village_1.name: Tân Lang Thôn
prov_r20_13_village_1.look: A coast village under tall straight areca palms, their nut clusters drying on mats.
prov_r20_13_village_1.lore: Its people sell areca nuts along the coast road; every guest is offered one at the door.

prov_r20_13_spirit_vein_2.name: Thâm Lục Mạch
prov_r20_13_spirit_vein_2.look: A hollow in the jungle where the leaves grow so thick and dark that it is green twilight at noon.
prov_r20_13_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein. Wood cultivators come to sit in the hollow and leave covered in moss.

prov_r20_14_town_1.name: Hương Liệu Thị
prov_r20_14_town_1.look: A small walled market town on the shore, its streets lined with sacks of pepper, cardamom and resin under awnings.
prov_r20_14_town_1.lore: The spice villages of the south coast bring their harvest here, and boats carry it on to Ngũ Thải and Thạch Cơ.

prov_r20_14_forest_2.name: Cổ Dung Lâm
prov_r20_14_forest_2.look: A jungle of vast banyans whose hanging roots have grown into whole new trunks, so that one tree looks like a forest.
prov_r20_14_forest_2.lore: The town's traders leave a coin in the roots of the oldest banyan before a voyage.

prov_r20_15_village_1.name: Sa Nhân Thôn
prov_r20_15_village_1.look: A shore village of thatched houses beside cardamom gardens planted in the shade of the jungle trees, with pods drying on woven trays in every yard.
prov_r20_15_village_1.lore: Its people grow cardamom under the canopy and sell the dried pods at Hương Liệu Thị. They will not walk on the grass shore by the old Xích Thành sea hall after dark.

prov_r20_15_spirit_vein_2.name: Tử Đàn Huyệt
prov_r20_15_spirit_vein_2.look: A ring of old rosewood trees in the jungle, their fallen leaves deep and dark underfoot.
prov_r20_15_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein lies under the ring. Phượng Minh forbids cutting the rosewood here.

prov_r20_15_ruin_3.name: Viêm Hải Quán
prov_r20_15_ruin_3.look: Broken red-stone halls on the grassy shore, their sea wall blackened as if by fire.
prov_r20_15_ruin_3.lore: A sea hall of Xích Thành Môn, where its disciples practised fire arts over the water. It was abandoned when the gate fell in 590, and Phượng Minh never reopened it.

prov_r20_16_town_1.name: Nam Tân Trấn
prov_r20_16_town_1.look: A small walled harbour town on a steep shore, its quay crowded with deep-sea boats.
prov_r20_16_town_1.lore: Boats sail from here to the far south and the islands. Its sailors say the great Bằng's wind starts at their quay.

prov_r20_16_forest_2.name: Mộc Miên Lâm
prov_r20_16_forest_2.look: A hillside of tall kapok trees that burst into huge red flowers on bare branches every spring.
prov_r20_16_forest_2.lore: The coast calls them hero trees. Their floss stuffs the town's pillows and sails' seams.

prov_r20_17_village_1.name: Đậu Khấu Thôn
prov_r20_17_village_1.look: A shore village among nutmeg trees on the jungle hills, brown seeds wrapped in red lace drying on mats in every yard.
prov_r20_17_village_1.lore: Its people grow nutmeg and mace and fish within sight of Thôn Hải's old islet. Their grandparents' grandparents came from the burned spice town of Hương Phàm, and every house keeps a charred plank from it over the hearth.

prov_r20_17_spirit_vein_2.name: Huyết Đằng Mạch
prov_r20_17_spirit_vein_2.look: A jungle hilltop knotted with vines as thick as an arm, which bleed dark red sap where they are cut.
prov_r20_17_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein runs under the hill and the vines grow fastest over it. Healers of the coast tap the sap to stop bleeding, and wood cultivators who sit here say they can feel the vines growing.

prov_r20_17_ruin_3.name: Hương Phàm Trấn
prov_r20_17_ruin_3.look: Charred walls among jungle on the shore, a burned quay running into the sea.
prov_r20_17_ruin_3.lore: A spice port of the south coast, burned by Thôn Hải's pirates in 771. The Purge came ten years too late for it, and its trade moved to Hương Liệu.

prov_r20_18_village_1.name: Bằng Trình Thôn
prov_r20_18_village_1.look: A jungle-edge fishing village whose long deep-sea boats are drawn up with their prows all pointing south.
prov_r20_18_village_1.lore: Its fishers sail further south than any others on the coast and say they follow the great Bằng's road.

prov_r20_18_spirit_vein_2.name: Nam Minh Mạch
prov_r20_18_spirit_vein_2.look: A rocky hilltop in the jungle with a clear spring that looks out over the open southern sea.
prov_r20_18_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Thủy (water) vein named for the southern deep where the Bằng flies in the old book. The spring always runs a little south.

prov_r20_19_village_1.name: Hồ Tiêu Thôn
prov_r20_19_village_1.look: A hill village above the sea where pepper vines climb every tree, and red and black berries dry on mats along the paths.
prov_r20_19_village_1.lore: Its people tend the vines on the jungle slope and carry the dried pepper down to the shore boats, which take it to Hương Liệu Thị and on to the cities. Every bride is given a vine to plant on her first day.

prov_r20_19_forest_2.name: Long Huyết Lâm
prov_r20_19_forest_2.look: Squat umbrella-shaped trees on a jungle slope, their cut bark weeping dark red resin.
prov_r20_19_forest_2.lore: Its resin, dragon's blood, is a medicine for wounds and a red varnish for the palace's zithers.

prov_r20_2_village_1.name: Lô Hội Thôn
prov_r20_2_village_1.look: A coast village of grass-roofed houses among rows of spiky grey-green aloe.
prov_r20_2_village_1.lore: Its people boil aloe into salve and sell it to Phần Vũ Đường for disciples burned in the vents.

prov_r20_2_spirit_vein_2.name: Dư Ôn Mạch
prov_r20_2_spirit_vein_2.look: A low grassy hill where snow-white ash shows in the soil and the ground is warm after dark.
prov_r20_2_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein running out from the vents to the north. Phần Vũ's disciples rest here between sittings.

prov_r20_20_village_1.name: Hồng Sa Thôn
prov_r20_20_village_1.look: A few fishing huts on a beach of red volcanic sand, boats drawn up above the tide.
prov_r20_20_village_1.lore: Its people fish and boil salt. Bathers come for the red sand, said to draw out fever.

prov_r20_20_hot_spring_2.name: Lãng Ôn Trì
prov_r20_20_hot_spring_2.look: A rock pool on the shore where hot water wells up through black rock and mixes with the breaking waves.
prov_r20_20_hot_spring_2.lore: At high tide it is warm, at low tide scalding; the villagers time their baths by the moon.

prov_r20_21_town_1.name: Thiên Nhai Trấn
prov_r20_21_town_1.gloss: Town at the Edge of the Sky
prov_r20_21_town_1.look: A small walled harbour town on a grassy cape, with nothing beyond it but sea.
prov_r20_21_town_1.lore: The last port before the open southern sea; ships take water here, and sailors carve their names on the quay before they leave.

prov_r20_21_beast_lair_2.name: Hỏa Tích Nhai
prov_r20_21_beast_lair_2.look: A black sea cliff beyond the town, its ledges crowded with great lizards basking in the sun.
prov_r20_21_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit monitor lizards that spit burning spittle nest here. The town's children are told never to climb it, and some do.

prov_r20_22_village_1.name: Thuận Phong Thôn
prov_r20_22_village_1.look: A jungle-edge fishing village facing a low grassy island across the strait.
prov_r20_22_village_1.lore: Its sailors row out to Đồ Nam Đảo to leave fish in the great Bằng's hollow for a fair wind south, and never sail without it.

prov_r20_23_village_1.name: Phù Thạch Thôn
prov_r20_23_village_1.look: A shore village under a smoking volcano, heaps of grey pumice stacked by every house.
prov_r20_23_village_1.lore: Its people gather pumice from the shore, where it floats in after each outburst, and sell it to masons and bath houses.

prov_r20_23_lava_vent_2.name: Luyện Vũ Huyệt
prov_r20_23_lava_vent_2.look: A red-glowing crack high on the volcano's flank, breathing heat over a bare slope of black rock.
prov_r20_23_lava_vent_2.lore: Phượng Minh holds it; its fire disciples come to temper their arts in the heat and say the vent forges feathers into flame. Its fire is Hỏa (fire) at its fiercest.

prov_r20_23_ruin_3.name: Lưu Hỏa Các
prov_r20_23_ruin_3.look: The upper halls of a red-stone pavilion jutting out of a tongue of black lava on the jungle slope.
prov_r20_23_ruin_3.lore: A fire hall of Xích Thành Môn, abandoned when the gate fell in 590. In 845 lava from the vent above ran down over its lower courts, and only its roofs still show.

prov_r20_24_village_1.name: Bái Nhật Thôn
prov_r20_24_village_1.gloss: Village That Bows to the Sun
prov_r20_24_village_1.look: A fishing village on the jungle shore whose people gather on the beach each dawn facing a forested island.
prov_r20_24_village_1.lore: Its fishers bow to the sunrise over Dục Nhật Đảo and ferry pilgrims to the hermit Mạc Quy Khư. They never fish the snake forest's creeks.

prov_r20_25_village_1.name: Phá Lãng Thôn
prov_r20_25_village_1.look: A jungle shore village of boatmen, its beach lined with small strong rowing boats.
prov_r20_25_village_1.lore: Its boatmen row treasure seekers out to Thôn Hải's islet to dig in the ash for Kình Nha, and charge for the trip both ways in advance.

prov_r20_25_forest_2.name: Thanh Gia Lâm
prov_r20_25_forest_2.look: A coastal grove of tall leaning coconut palms above a white beach.
prov_r20_25_forest_2.lore: Its palms give the village rope, oil and roofing; the boatmen say no pirate ever hid in it.

prov_r20_3_village_1.name: Trúc Lâu Thôn
prov_r20_3_village_1.look: A coast village of raised bamboo houses on stilts among rice and mulberry plots.
prov_r20_3_village_1.lore: Its people grow rice and mulberry, and lately sell their cocoons to the weavers on the shore.

prov_r20_3_spirit_vein_2.name: Thanh Can Mạch
prov_r20_3_spirit_vein_2.look: A bamboo grove near the shore whose green canes grow twice as thick as any around it, creaking in the sea wind.
prov_r20_3_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein lies under the grove. The villagers of Trúc Lâu cut its canes only for the main posts of their houses, and the weavers of Chức Hà Các come here to sit before a new loom is strung.

prov_r20_3_minor_seat_p.name: Chức Hà Các
prov_r20_3_minor_seat_p.look: A long red-timber pavilion on the grassy shore, its open halls hung with bolts of silk that glow red at dusk.
prov_r20_3_minor_seat_p.lore: A minor sect of weavers sworn to Phượng Minh, founded in 1150, which weaves fire-silk robes and banners from Tang Điền's worms without the vents. It says it has rediscovered Xích Thành's lost craft by other means, and the palace has not yet decided whether that pleases it.

prov_r20_4_village_1.name: Cam Giá Thôn
prov_r20_4_village_1.look: A shore village surrounded by tall sugarcane, with an ox-driven cane press and a smoking boiling shed at its centre.
prov_r20_4_village_1.lore: Its people crush the cane in the press, boil the juice down into cakes of brown sugar and ship them to Ngũ Thải and the cities. They start the boiling with water from the hot spring in the fields, which saves a day's firewood.

prov_r20_4_hot_spring_2.name: Phí Thạch Thang
prov_r20_4_hot_spring_2.look: A spring in the cane fields that boils hard among white stones, steaming day and night.
prov_r20_4_hot_spring_2.lore: The villagers start the cane boiling with its water and cook eggs in it for travellers.

prov_r20_5_village_1.name: Lam Điện Thôn
prov_r20_5_village_1.look: A shore village where vats of blue dye stand in every yard and cloth dries in long blue banners.
prov_r20_5_village_1.lore: Its people grow indigo and dye cloth and silk; their hands are blue to the wrist.

prov_r20_5_hot_spring_2.name: Lục Phàn Trì
prov_r20_5_hot_spring_2.look: A warm pool in the grass whose water is a cloudy green and whose rim is crusted with green crystals.
prov_r20_5_hot_spring_2.lore: The dyers scrape its green vitriol to fix their colours, and alchemists buy it too.

prov_r20_5_ruin_3.name: Kim Sa Trấn
prov_r20_5_ruin_3.look: Sand-drifted walls on the shore, the lower streets under the sea at high tide.
prov_r20_5_ruin_3.lore: A fishing and trading town on the golden beach, drowned by a great storm tide in 913. Its people moved inland, and their grandchildren became the dyers of Lam Điện.

prov_r20_6_village_1.name: Lệ Chi Thôn
prov_r20_6_village_1.look: A shore village among lychee orchards, its trees hung with red fruit in early summer.
prov_r20_6_village_1.lore: Its lychees are rushed to the cities by fast boat, since they spoil in three days.

prov_r20_6_forest_2.name: Phượng Vĩ Lâm
prov_r20_6_forest_2.look: A stand of spreading flame trees on the grass, their crowns blazing scarlet every summer.
prov_r20_6_forest_2.lore: The coast calls them phoenix-tail trees. Phượng Minh's disciples collect the fallen flowers for the summer rites.

prov_r20_7_village_1.name: Quế Viên Thôn
prov_r20_7_village_1.look: A jungle village in a clearing of longan orchards, the brown fruit drying over smoky charcoal racks under long open sheds.
prov_r20_7_village_1.lore: Its people dry longans into the sweet brown rounds sold in every market of the coast, and burn the pruned wood into charcoal. They keep torches lit in the orchards at night against the flying foxes of the valley nearby.

prov_r20_7_beast_lair_2.name: Phi Hồ Cốc
prov_r20_7_beast_lair_2.look: A jungle valley where the trees hang black with thousands of roosting giant bats.
prov_r20_7_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit flying foxes with wings wider than a man's arms roost here by day and strip the orchards by night.

prov_r20_7_ruin_3.name: Bàn Căn Trấn
prov_r20_7_ruin_3.look: Burned stilts and walls among mangrove roots on the shore, half swallowed by the tide.
prov_r20_7_ruin_3.lore: A mangrove town of fishers and charcoal burners, burned by Thôn Hải's raiders in 767. The mangroves have taken it back.

prov_r20_8_village_1.name: Bạch Diêm Thôn
prov_r20_8_village_1.look: A flat coast village beside a grid of salt pans gleaming white in the sun.
prov_r20_8_village_1.lore: Its people make salt and fish the shallows; its salt is whiter than any on the coast.

prov_r20_8_spirit_vein_2.name: Triều Căn Nhãn
prov_r20_8_spirit_vein_2.look: A clear pool among mangrove roots inland, where the water rises and falls with no channel to the sea.
prov_r20_8_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Thủy (water) vein. Phượng Minh's scholars have added it to the puzzle of Hồ Tâm's lake.

prov_r20_9_peak_1.name: Thải Phượng Phong
prov_r20_9_peak_1.look: A tall red crag above the west coast, its rock banded in red, yellow and grey.
prov_r20_9_peak_1.lore: It is said the five-coloured bird was seen over this peak in the old days, and the coast was named for it. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).
